summary: 1. Use sensory mental imagery in the first 3 seconds (e.g., 'socho, tumhare daanto par 3 chhoti cars...') rather than reading a generic question or technical description. 2. Frame titles as short Hinglish direct questions featuring visual real-world objects (Car, T. rex) with a relevant emoji. 3. Avoid full English formal titles which collapsed stayed_pct down to 6.7%. 4. Focus topics on physical, tangible mechanics or extreme scale comparisons rather than abstract scientific phenomena. 5. Keep video scripts concise enough to deliver high payoff before viewer attention drops.
winning_hooks: Start immediately with 'Socho...' followed by a concrete, extreme visual visual scale (e.g., 3 cars stacked on teeth).
State a direct counter-intuitive fact upfront (e.g., 'Jo car crash mein pichak jaati hai, woh tumhein zyada bachati hai').
avoid: Dry formal Hindi or pure English title phrasing ('Common Household Items That Contain...').
Hooking with long academic explanations before setting up a visceral visual hook.
next_experiment: A/B test the exact same topic using a visual imagination hook ('Socho...') vs a counter-intuitive assertion hook ('Did you know...'), keeping title in short Hinglish question format.
